deities: Lord Dattatreya (combined form of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)

history.period: Traditional site; current shrine's construction date not documented
history.summary: The Dattatreya temple stands at the summit of Mount Girnar near Junagadh, reached by a climb of ~10,000 steps from the base (ropeway runs to the Ambaji temple, from where ~4,000 steps remain). Tradition holds that Lord Dattatreya left home young and meditated on this peak for 12,000 years; the shrine holds the imprints (paduka) of his lotus feet rather than a full idol, and the Sansthan runs a 24x7 free-meal service for pilgrims. NOTE: Wikipedia's Girnar article records a contested Jain claim that the summit shrine was formerly a Neminath temple 'illegally converted' to a Dattatreya temple (see seq 289, Girnar Jain Temples); this dispute is unresolved in sources consulted. Opening hours conflict: 7 AM-7 PM (several sources) vs 8 AM-6 PM (YatraDham). Coordinates (21.528321, 70.533486) from the Sansthan's own listing, corroborated by a nearby map pin (21.528119, 70.533527).

name: Shri Guru Dattatreya Mandir, Girnar
town_description: Junagadh is a historic city in Gujarat's Saurashtra region, nestled at the foot of Mount Girnar. Its past stretches from Ashoka's 3rd-century BCE rock edicts and the Uparkot Fort to the Nawabi-era Mahabat Maqbara, and it is a major pilgrimage hub for both Hindus and Jains.

travel.airport: Keshod (~40 km) or Rajkot (~103 km) from Junagadh
travel.railway: Junagadh Junction (~6 km from Girnar Taleti, the base)
travel.road: Girnar Taleti base reached by road from Junagadh; summit by ~10,000 steps or ropeway to Ambaji plus ~4,000 steps

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; start the climb early morning to beat heat and return before dusk
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7 AM-7 PM (multiple sources; YatraDham lists 8 AM-6 PM — verify before visiting)
